chunk_findings.detail: `export_targets` is purely config-driven (`[p for _doc, p, _mode in cfg.export.targets()]`) and performs no marker inspection, yet `doc_exclude` uses it to suppress the stale-mention scan (and, per the stated intent, docscheck) for those paths. The enforce generalisation only treats a file as generated when its first line carries the `ddflow:generated` marker with a known doc kind, and the stated acceptance case is precisely "a hand-written file with a region is not treated as a generated file" — i.e. an export target can exist on disk without the marker. For such a target, `export --check` will not judge it (no marker), but `doc_exclude(cfg)` still removes it from `docsync.stale_mentions`/docscheck, so a stale mention inside it is never reported anywhere. Given config with an export target `docs/hand.md` whose first line is a region marker but no `ddflow:generated`, committing a change that makes a stale mention in `docs/hand.md` true yields no diagnostic under `[enforce].stale_docs = block`, because both the view check (marker absent) and the stale-mention scan (path excluded) skip it. The exclusion should be restricted to targets that actually carry the generated marker, or the docstring's claim that these are "generated documents" is not what the code implements.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/shared_files.py `export_targets` / `doc_exclude`

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `run_cli(proj, "export", "enable", "roadmap", "--path", "NOTES.md", "--mode", "region")[0] in (0, 3)` accepts exit status 3 as well as 0. If `export enable --mode region` exits 3 (unsupported mode, target not registered, no-op), then `NOTES.md` is never an export target at all, and the assertions that follow (lines 130–131: overwrite with an arbitrary `ddflow:begin` region, then `_commit(...).returncode == 0`) become vacuous — a plain markdown file whose first line is `# Notes` commits successfully even with no `check_views` change whatsoever, because it never carried the `ddflow:generated` first-line marker. The acceptance criterion is "failing-first"; with this leniency the test can pass in the pre-change state and therefore does not actually exercise the generalization it claims to guard.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_enforce.py:124 (`test_a_hand_written_file_with_a_region_is_not_a_generated_file`)

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture writes `commit_without_lease = "off"` for every test, which disables lease enforcement entirely. The stated acceptance that export targets are "excluded from lease checks" is thus never exercised: the only lease-related assertion in the file, `assert DOC not in cfg.lease.shared_globs` (line 180), inspects config contents, not enforcement. Given a regression in which a staged export target incorrectly demands a lease (e.g. because the auto-registered shared glob is treated as lease-relevant), every test in this file still passes, because no commit in the suite ever runs with the lease check enabled (e.g. `commit_without_lease = "block"`). The claim is therefore untested by this change.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_enforce.py:46 (`_config` / `proj` fixture) and tests/test_export_enforce.py:180

chunk_findings.detail: The diagnostic label is derived from *one* of the two result sets rather than from what is actually staged. A single commit can stage both kinds — e.g. `git add docs/roadmap.md docs/export/notes.md` where the event log has changes the commit does not record. `_staged_generated` then returns a non-empty `staged` *and* a non-empty `exports`, so `staged` is truthy and `noun` becomes `"generated view"`. Both verdict paths that use it (`"ddflow: a {noun} is staged, but git could not report the state of the event log ..."` and `"ddflow: a {noun} is staged, but the event log it is rendered from has N change(s) the commit does not record:"`) therefore describe the staged export as a view / omit it entirely, even though the export is the (or an) artifact the check is blocking on. The label should be derived from `exports`/`staged` jointly (or the messages emitted per kind), otherwise the user-facing block reason for a mixed stage is factually incomplete about what is staged.

chunk_findings.detail: The assertion `"PROBLEM" not in out.split("ROADMAP.md (roadmap)")[0].splitlines()[-1]` does not reliably check that the stale-target report is a NOTE rather than a PROBLEM. If the stale note is the first line of doctor output, the split head is empty, `.splitlines()` is `[]`, and `[-1]` raises `IndexError`, failing the test with a crash instead of an assertion. If there is a blank line before the note, `splitlines()[-1]` is `""`, so the test silently passes even when a `PROBLEM` header appeared earlier in the output. The test therefore both false-errors and false-passes depending on doctor’s formatting.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_export_enforce.py:149

chunk_findings.detail: `assert "no merge strategy" not in out or DOC not in out.split("no merge strategy")[0][-200:]` does not actually assert that doctor emitted no “no merge strategy” note for the registered export target. Given output such as `no merge strategy for ROADMAP.md`, the left side is false and the right side is `"ROADMAP.md" not in ""`, which is true, so the assertion passes despite the forbidden note. It only catches the case where `DOC` appears before the phrase within the previous 200 characters, so the stated acceptance criterion can regress without this test failing.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test registers a *region-mode* (i.e. partially hand-written) export target `NOTES.md` and then asserts `"NOTES.md" in shared_globs(Config.load(proj))`. The sibling test `test_export_targets_are_shared_and_draw_no_merge_note` demonstrates the consequence of membership in `shared_globs`: `conflicts([DOC], [DOC], shared_globs(cfg)) == []` ("no claim on it is needed") and the doctor "no merge strategy" note is suppressed. So for the region target the change makes a file the test itself describes as *not* generated — the comment right above says "its hand-written text is still scanned by stale_docs / docscheck: only whole files are excluded" — be treated as a shared, regenerable artifact for lease purposes. Concrete scenario: lease A and lease B both edit the hand-written portion of `NOTES.md`; `conflicts([... "NOTES.md" ...], [... "NOTES.md" ...], shared_globs(cfg))` returns `[]`, so the second lease is never flagged and doctor emits no "no merge strategy" warning, and one agent's hand-written edits can be silently overwritten. Only whole-file generated targets are self-contained enough to justify being dropped from conflict detection; a region-mode target containing hand-written text should stay claim-protected (and note-producing), just as it stays in `doc_exclude`'s complement. The assertion `"NOTES.md" in shared_globs(...)` therefore encodes the wrong behavior (or, if the implementation only registers whole-file targets, is a failing assertion).
